title: Finite-diagonal Hom totalization of exact columns is acyclic
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and let $E,A$ be cochain complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose integers $N,M$ satisfy $E^p=0$ for $p>N$ and $A^q=0$ for $q<M$. For every pair of integers $p,q$, suppose the short complex $\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^{q-1})\to\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^q)\to\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^{q+1})$, with maps induced by $d_A$, is exact at its middle term. Then the total sheaf Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,A)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. No freeness or separate acyclicity assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 via Tag 0GM7, case (2); explicit finite-free Hom calculation

proof.text: fix a degree n and bounds N for E and M for A. A total cocycle has components only for M-n ≤ p ≤ N. Set the degree n-1 primitive to zero above N and descend in p. If the equation at p+1 has been solved, subtract the signed precomposition of that primitive with d_E from the p-th cocycle component. The cocycle equation, the equation at p+1 and d_E squared equal to zero show that this obstruction lies in the kernel of postcomposition with d_A. Exactness of the internal-Hom column at q=p+n gives a local lift along d_A from degree q-1. Perform only the finitely many lifts with M-n+1 ≤ p ≤ N, taking a common refinement of their coverings. At p=M-n the column's incoming object is zero, so exactness forces the remaining obstruction to be zero. Below that degree both cocycle and primitive components vanish. Thus on the resulting covering the total differential of the primitive is the given cocycle. The local exactness criterion for module sheaves gives exactness in degree n; n was arbitrary. This uses the product and signed differential characterization of homComplex_exists, and is valid even if the interval of possible components is empty.
